subject: Clarifications: model catalog licensing, pinning, and operator responsibilities
messages:
From: Liz Wong <liz.wong@northbridge.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: model catalog licensing + pinning questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We're working through the model catalog & licensing section of the questionnaire and have a few clarifying questions before we complete the form:

1) For open-source upstreams, can you provide the chain-of-custody you maintain? Specifically we need: the upstream repo/commit, any fork or conversion steps, and the license reconciliation that led to final catalog classification.

2) How do you handle version pinning for customer deployments? We want to know whether pinning is operator-managed (Redwood) or customer-managed, whether pins are "soft" (auto-update with notice) or "hard" (no auto-update), and what escalation/rollback mechanisms exist.

3) What notification cadence do you provide when a model's upstream license or security advisory changes? We typically need a minimum of 14 days notice before a required change is applied to production.

4) Do you publish cryptographic hashes or signed attestations for catalog artifacts so our security team can independently verify integrity?

Attach: the RFI spreadsheet (we've included the section in Column F) — please respond inline if possible.

Best,
Liz Wong
Senior Procurement Manager
Northbridge Financial

---
Note: Filling this out is a gating item for our compliance review. If helpful we can schedule a quick operator-level call next week.
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Liz Wong <liz.wong@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog licensing + pinning questions

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Marissa and Neha are looped for technical detail and formal text we can paste into the RFI. We'll also attach a draft manifest that shows fields we keep in the catalog for every model.

Quick answers:
- Chain-of-custody: we track upstream repo, commit hash, the build that produced the artifact, and any conversion/quantization steps. We keep a change log and license reconciliation notes per artifact.
- Pinning: customers can choose the pining mode at deployment time. Our default for hosted customers is a "soft pin" (auto-update with 14-day advisory) unless a customer elects a hard pin. For Dedicated/Private contracts we support enforced hard pins.
- Notifications: we provide programmatic change advisories (email + webhook) at configurable windows (14/7/3 days) and publish signed advisories when changes are security-critical or license-affecting.
- Signatures/hashes: yes — every catalog artifact has a SHA256 hash, and for Private deployments we can enable signed attestations via your KMS.

Attachments: catalog_manifest_v1.json (sample), RFI_answers_draft.docx (work-in-progress).

Marissa/Neha — can you add the technical language around SBOMs, attestations, and the pin lifecycle we typically include in enterprise RFIs? Also call out operator responsibilities vs customer responsibilities for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liz Wong <liz.wong@northbridge.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog licensing + pinning questions

Hi Liz — following up with the more formal text you can paste into Column F. I'm keeping it concrete to match your compliance checklist.

(1) Catalog provenance and chain-of-custody
- For every cataloged model artifact we record: upstream_source (URL), upstream_commit (SHA or tag), source_license (SPDX identifier), conversion_steps (e.g., ONNX conversion, int8 quantization) with actor identity (automation account or human), and build_identifier (artifact id).
- We persist an immutable provenance record in our catalog service. For Hosted deployments the record is available via a read-only API and is included in exports. For Dedicated/Private we surface the same data into the customer's private control plane.
- We also generate a plain-text SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) listing associated weights, tokenizer, and third-party components. Sample SBOM attached (model-sbom-sample.txt).

(2) Licensing reconciliation and classification
- We run automated SPDX-based license detection across upstream sources. Any ambiguous cases are escalated to our legal intake. Final catalog classification is stored as spdx_final and includes a short rationale and timestamp.
- If an upstream license changes in a way that affects downstream rights, we mark the catalog entry as "license-affected" and publish an advisory.

(3) Pinning lifecycle and operator vs customer controls
- Pin modes available at deployment:
  * Soft pin (default hosted): model will auto-update to compatible, non-breaking patch releases. Auto-update triggers a notification workflow: advisory at 14/7/3 days and a pre-rollout canary for 5% traffic. Customers may opt-out via console toggle.
  * Hard pin (recommended for regulated workloads): model is pinned to a specific artifact id; no automatic updates. Rollouts to a new artifact require an explicit orchestrated upgrade and customer acceptance.
  * Managed pin (Dedicated): Redwood operators may manage pins under a customer-authorized runbook (common for larger installs). Runbooks include smoke-test suites and automatic rollback windows.
- Rollback and escalation: rollouts include automatic health checks and immediate rollback on quality or latency regressions; operator escalation channels include 24x7 oncall for Dedicated customers per SLA.

(4) Notifications, advisories, and signed attestations
- We publish programmatic advisories for license/security changes. Advisory metadata: advisory_id, affected_artifacts, classification (security/license), severity, recommended_action, and timeline.
- Cryptographic integrity: each artifact has a published SHA256 and we optionally sign attestations using Redwood's code-signing key. For Private customers we offer attestations signed by the customer's KMS via an integration.

(5) Operational details we recommend you include in contract
- Notification windows (14/7/3) for non-critical changes, immediate alerting for critical security advisories.
- Acceptance window for hard-pin upgrades (recommended 30 days).
- Right to request SBOMs and signed attestations on demand (contract clause).

I can paste this into your RFI file if you want — Sean, if you're happy with wording we'll push a polished draft to RFI_answers_draft.docx.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Catalog & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
On style: we avoid legalese in the RFI but include precise observability fields so your security team can verify programmatically.
From: Liz Wong <liz.wong@northbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog licensing + pinning questions

Marissa — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of follow-ups from Security:

A) Can you confirm the cryptographic signature model? Is the signature applied at the artifact level and published alongside the manifest? If so, do you publish the cert chain and do you rotate signing keys?

B) For the 14/7/3 advisory windows — are those configurable per-deployment? We need the ability to extend the window for sensitive customers to 30/14/7.

C) For Private deployments we want to ensure the SBOM export does not leak any Redwood-internal metadata. Is there an option to sanitize provenance fields for exports?

If you can provide short answers to A-C I can finalize Column F and mark this gating item as done. Thanks again.

--
Liz Wong
Senior Procurement Manager
Northbridge Financial
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Liz Wong <liz.wong@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog licensing + pinning questions (final)

Liz — final answers inline:

A) Signing model: signatures are applied per-artifact and published adjacent to the manifest. We publish SHA256 and an associated signature blob (base64) plus a signing-key-id. For hosted advisories we publish Redwood's signing cert chain. Keys are rotated on a schedule and key-ids are versioned in the advisory metadata. For Private deployments we can optionally use your KMS to sign artifacts; in that case the cert chain is controlled by you.

B) Advisory windows: yes, advisory cadence is configurable per-deployment. Console and API allow setting custom windows (e.g., 30/14/7). Default remains 14/7/3 for hosted customers.

C) SBOM export sanitization: yes. For Private exports we support a "sanitize_internal" flag that strips Redwood-internal actor IDs and automation account names from the exported provenance. The SBOM still retains upstream source URLs, commit SHAs, and license identifiers.

Next steps: I'll drop the polished answers into RFI_answers_draft.docx and share a HubSpot task for legal review. If you want a short operator-level call to walk through the signing/kms flow we can do 30 minutes next week.

Attachments (sent): catalog_manifest_v1.json, model-sbom-sample.txt, RFI_answers_draft.docx
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/NB-2027-INV-4421

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation so we can close the gating item.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
